5. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Aman Khan, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.
322 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 368 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, registered at P.S.
Jagdishpura, District Agra.
6.

The FIR of the matter was lodged on 02.06.2022 under Sections 363, 366 IPC by Omprakash Kushwaha against the applicant alleging therein that on 02.06.2022 at about 03:15 pm the applicant lured and enticed his daughter aged about 13 years studying in class 7th.
They were seen going by one Rajveer.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the victim was subjected to medical examination and no internal or external injuries were found on her person.
It is argued that the victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she went with the applicant out of her own sweet will.
It is further argued that in the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. of the victim, she states that on a false promise to marry the applicant established physical relationship with her.

He further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 20 of the affidavit and is in jail since 29.06.2022.
8.

Per contra, learned counsel for the first informant and learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is named in the FIR, statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim and role has been assigned.
It is argued that during investigation Sections 376, 368 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act has been added in the matter.
It is argued that since the victim is a minor, her statements cannot be looked into at this stage.
It is argued that there is no reason for false implication of the applicant and as such the prayer for bail of the applicant be rejected.
9. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the victim is aged about 13 years as per FIR and school records.

The applicant is named in the FIR,
statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim and role has been assigned.
The consent of a minor is of no worth.
I do not find it a fit case for bail.
10. Considering the totality of the case in particular, nature of evidence available on record, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
11. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023 M. ARIF (Samit Gopal, J.)
